source.original_text: The actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian mixtures satisfy the full quantitative single-block TV separation. \mathrm{TV}(P_+,P_-)\ge\frac{q^n}{2+4ns/(s+1)^2}\ge\frac12\exp\!\left(-\frac{5n}{s}\right),\qquad s=\sqrt\kappa,\quad q=\frac{s-1}{s+1}. Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\). No parity restriction; every \(n/2\) in the proof is real. \(\mu\) is normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\), with both determinant signs. The two priors are exactly twice its restrictions to \(\det O=\pm1\); \(P_\pm\) are the actual Gaussian bind mixtures defined below. TV is the normalized supremum over measurable Euclidean events. Probability, kernel measurability, finite real event mass, integrability, the selected parameter signs, Eq24 and the scalar estimates are produced internally. None is a caller hypothesis. A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top),\quad\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1}),\quad\nu_\pm=2\mu\!\restriction\{\det O=\pm1\},\quad P_\pm=\nu_\pm\mathrm{bind}\gamma. \begin{aligned}\delta&=\sup_{B\text{ measurable}}|P_+(B)-P_-(B)|,&s&=\sqrt\kappa,&q&=\frac{s-1}{s+1},\\a&=1-\frac1n,&r&=aq,&\ell&=\frac{4ns+(s-1)^2}{8n(n-1)},&D&=2+\frac{4ns}{(s+1)^2}.\end{aligned}

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with n ≥ 3 and every real number κ with κ ≥ 4, make the following definitions. Let s = √κ, where √ is the real square root. Let G = O(n), the full group of real orthogonal n × n matrices, including both determinant signs, and let μ be the canonical normalized Haar probability measure on G. Write Q(O) for the real matrix underlying O ∈ G. Define measures on G by
ν₊ = 2 μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det Q(O) = 1},
ν₋ = 2 μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det Q(O) = −1}.
The factors 2 in these measure definitions are extended nonnegative real scalars.
For O ∈ G, define the real n × n matrices
A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(Q(O) + Q(O)ᵀ),
C(O) = A(O)⁻¹,
and define γ(O) = multivariateGaussian(0, C(O)) on real n-dimensional Euclidean space. The matrix inverse here is the standard totalized matrix inverse. Precisely, the Gaussian constructor means the pushforward of canonical standard Gaussian measure by z ↦ 0 + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM(CFC.sqrt(C(O))) z; its covariance interpretation is the one supplied for positive semidefinite matrix arguments.
Let P₊ = ν₊.bind γ and P₋ = ν₋.bind γ, so these measures are obtained by integrating the displayed Gaussian measure γ(O) against the respective determinant-sign measures. Define the real number
δ = sup { |P₊.real(B) − P₋.real(B)| : B is a Borel measurable subset of real n-dimensional Euclidean space },
where P.real(B) is the extended nonnegative measure of B converted to a real number, and the supremum is the real sSup operator. Equivalently, the set whose sSup is taken consists of the real numbers z for which there exists a Borel measurable B with z = |P₊.real(B) − P₋.real(B)|.
Then both of the following weak inequalities hold:
(1/2) exp(−5n/s) ≤ ((s − 1)/(s + 1))ⁿ / (2 + 4ns/(s + 1)²),
((s − 1)/(s + 1))ⁿ / (2 + 4ns/(s + 1)²) ≤ δ.
Here n is converted to a real number in the exponential and the denominator, whereas the powers with exponent n are natural-number powers. Real division and inverse use their totalized Lean meanings. No attainment of the supremum, upper bound on δ, or additional universal parameter is part of this conclusion.

/-!
# Actual single-block separation

Proposition B.7, Eq19 of Zhou--Suzuki, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
The source's actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian mixtures have normalized
event TV at least the explicit ratio, and hence the stated exponential.
Eq20, Eq24 and the scalar exponential comparison are reused canonical nodes.
The remaining Bernoulli and denominator estimates are discharged internally.
This single-block result does not assert amplification, transcript/oracle,
query-cap, precision, expected-cost, hidden-eigenbasis or main lower bounds.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.SingleBlockSeparation
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem single_block_separation {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    let μ := orthogonalHaar n
    let νpos := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = 1}
    let νneg := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • μ.restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = -1}
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
    let Ppos := νpos.bind γ
    let Pneg := νneg.bind γ
    let δ : ℝ := sSup {z : ℝ | ∃ B : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)),
      MeasurableSet B ∧ z = |Ppos.real B - Pneg.real B|}
    (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(5 * (n : ℝ)) / s) ≤
      (((s - 1) / (s + 1)) ^ n) /
        (2 + 4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2) ∧
    (((s - 1) / (s + 1)) ^ n) /
        (2 + 4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2) ≤ δ := by
  dsimp only
  constructor
  · exact NumericSeparation.explicit_ratio_ge_exponential hn hκ
  · let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    let q : ℝ := (s - 1) / (s + 1)
    let a : ℝ := 1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)
    let r : ℝ := a * q
    let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
      (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
    let v : ℝ := ((-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (n : ℝ)) * q ^ n *
      a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - r ^ 2)
    have hn3 : (3 : ℝ) ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hn0 : (0 : ℝ) < n := by linarith
    have hs : (2 : ℝ) ≤ s := Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le (by linarith)
    have hsp : 0 < s + 1 := by linarith
    have hq : 0 < q := div_pos (by linarith) hsp
    have hq1 : q < 1 := (div_lt_one hsp).2 (by linarith)
    have hqn : 0 ≤ q ^ n := (pow_pos hq n).le
    have hinv0 : 0 < 1 / (n : ℝ) := one_div_pos.mpr hn0
    have hinv1 : 1 / (n : ℝ) < 1 := (div_lt_one hn0).2 (by linarith)
    have ha : 0 < a := by dsimp [a]; linarith
    have hpow : 0 < a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos ha _
    have ht := SelectedTilt.selected_tilt hn hκ
    have hr : 0 < r := ht.1
    have hr1 : r < 1 := ht.2.1
    have hden : 0 < 1 - r ^ 2 := by nlinarith
    have hprod : 0 < (n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2) := mul_pos hn0 hden
    -- Bernoulli uses a real exponent, including odd dimensions.
    have hhalf : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) := by
      have hb := one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add
        (s := -(1 / (n : ℝ))) (by linarith : -1 ≤ -(1 / (n : ℝ)))
        (p := (n : ℝ) / 2) (by linarith : 1 ≤ (n : ℝ) / 2)
      have hlin : (1 : ℝ) + (n : ℝ) / 2 * (-(1 / (n : ℝ))) = 1 / 2 := by
        field_simp
        ring
      rw [hlin] at hb
      simpa only [a, sub_eq_add_neg] using hb
    -- The literal denominator identity is the source's unnumbered display.
    have hdenid : (n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2) =
        4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2 + q ^ 2 * (2 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) := by
      dsimp only [r, a, q]
      field_simp
      ring
    have hq2 : q ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by nlinarith
    have hterm : q ^ 2 * (2 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ≤ 2 := by
      have hm : 0 ≤ 2 - 1 / (n : ℝ) := by linarith
      have hu := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hq2 hm
      nlinarith
    have hdenle : (n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2) ≤
        2 + 4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2 := by linarith [hdenid]
    have hD : 0 < 2 + 4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2 := by positivity
    -- Absolute value removes (-1)^n without a parity restriction.
    have hvabs : |v| = q ^ n * a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) /
        ((n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2)) := by
      simp only [v, abs_div, abs_mul, abs_pow, abs_neg, abs_one, one_pow,
        abs_of_pos hn0, abs_of_nonneg hq.le, abs_of_pos hpow, abs_of_pos hden]
      field_simp
    have hratio : q ^ n / (2 + 4 * (n : ℝ) * s / (s + 1) ^ 2) ≤
        q ^ n / ((n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2)) :=
      (div_le_div_iff₀ hD hprod).2 (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hdenle hqn)
    have htest : q ^ n / ((n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2)) ≤ 2 * |v| := by
      rw [hvabs]
      have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hhalf hqn
      have hnum : q ^ n ≤ 2 * (q ^ n * a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) := by nlinarith
      calc
        _ ≤ (2 * (q ^ n * a ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2))) /
            ((n : ℝ) * (1 - r ^ 2)) := div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hnum hprod.le
        _ = _ := by ring
    have he := EvaluatedGaussian.selected_gaussian_value hn hκ
    have htv := ActualTotalVariation.actual_radial_test_tv hn hκ (ℓ := ℓ) ht.2.2.1.le
    dsimp only at he htv
    rw [he.2.2.2] at htv
    change 2 * |v| ≤ _ at htv
    exact hratio.trans (htest.trans htv)

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.SingleBlockSeparation

notation.text: A is precision, so its inverse is covariance. The group is the full orthogonal group; its determinant sign is distinct from positive definiteness of A.
The event supremum is over all Borel measurable subsets of real n-dimensional Euclidean space. Selected parameters are definitions depending only on n and κ.

steps.title: Use the actual radial-test bound
steps.text: The selected tilt is positive. Apply the canonical Eq20 theorem to the literal Gaussian mixtures and the bounded test. Its probability, density, L1 and event-supremum adapters remain inside that parent.
steps.lean: ht is SelectedTilt.selected_tilt hn hκ; htv is ActualTotalVariation.actual_radial_test_tv hn hκ at ht.2.2.1.le. No abstract TV bound or test expectation is supplied.

steps.title: Insert the evaluated expectation
steps.text: Use the single canonical Eq24 value. All positive factors are proved from the source range. Taking absolute value removes the parity sign for every n.
steps.lean: he is EvaluatedGaussian.selected_gaussian_value hn hκ; rw [he.2.2.2] identifies the literal density integral. hvabs simplifies absolute values, using hq, hpow, hn0 and hden, without an even-dimension assumption.

steps.title: Keep the real half-power factor
steps.text: Bernoulli’s inequality applies because the real exponent n/2 is at least one and the increment −1/n is at least −1. Its linear term is exactly one half.
steps.lean: hhalf calls the existing Mathlib one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add. hlin cancels the nonzero real n. This implements source Ex62 and does not introduce a new general wrapper.

steps.title: Bound the exact denominator
steps.text: Expand the literal selected r. Since 0<q<1 and 0≤2−1/n≤2, the remaining product is at most two.
steps.lean: hdenid is the exact Ex63 identity; hq2 and hterm give hdenle. hprod and hD establish the strict positivity needed to reverse the denominator order.

steps.title: Obtain the rational TV separation
steps.text: Combine the two scalar estimates with the actual test bound. Both denominator comparisons use positive quantities.
steps.lean: hratio consumes hdenle via div_le_div_iff₀; htest consumes hhalf and hvabs; their transitive composition with htv proves the new actual rational bound, source Ex64.

steps.title: Reuse the exponential comparison
steps.text: The existing canonical scalar theorem supplies the second source inequality with the same constant five. Its proof uses two standard log tangent bounds, an explicitly recorded alternative sufficient proof of the author’s integral estimate; this packet does not reprove it.
steps.lean: The first conjunction calls NumericSeparation.explicit_ratio_ge_exponential hn hκ directly. The active source projection stops at that canonical parent while the full author route remains in the expanded source graph.

steps.title: Consume an odd-dimensional source endpoint
steps.text: At n=3 and κ=4, the actual target measures have a strictly positive TV lower bound and cannot be equal. An even-dimensional non-boundary example is checked as well.
steps.lean: Tests/GaussianComplexitySingleBlockSeparation.lean instantiates the actual bind measures. If the two n=3 measures were equal the event-gap set would be {0}, contradicting the compiled lower bound.
